correctness.rationale: The three triggers and the FJR and EJR+ quantifiers match the cited definitions. In the witness voter 3's maximum satisfaction fixes every chosen candidate; group {1,2} violates only the cohesion equality trigger for target one. It has no common approved candidate, and its singleton subgroups have cohesion entitlement zero. FJR has benchmark zero for those singletons (pick an empty-approval round at full horizon); for the pair, a one-round choice cannot satisfy both, and for the full horizon the two identical first rounds witness benchmark zero. With two voters, a non-maximal supporter count is Pareto-dominated roundwise, so the grand-coalition score is maximal; singleton FJR+ triggers are covered by EJR+. For three voters and at most two rounds, singleton triggers cannot occur; pair triggers require two unanimous pair rounds, hence EJR+ protects target one; a grand-coalition violation would require all-zero satisfaction at target one or two unanimous rounds at target two, both inconsistent with Pareto efficiency and the trigger. For one candidate the maximal total support equals actual total satisfaction on every group. Independent witness evaluation and 1056 reduced profile/outcome checks agree (python /workspace/independent_checks.py 2). The short-domain replay reduces arbitrary candidate sets to maximal supporter masks: dropping smaller masks preserves common-approval availability, per-round support maxima and Pareto comparisons, and no Pareto-efficient outcome chooses such a smaller mask.
residual_risks: The universal two-voter argument is a proof, not an extrapolation from finite checks. The witness uses empty ballots; no minimum in the mandatory nonempty-ballot domain is established.
